name: to_dense
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::to_dense(Tensor self, ScalarType? dtype=None, *, bool? masked_grad=None) -> Tensor. This representative signature is not exclusive. All registered schemas supplied for this operator, verbatim: aten::to_dense(Tensor self, ScalarType? dtype=None, *, bool? masked_grad=None) -> Tensor. Semantics derived from the tests: to_dense densifies a sparse input (COO, CSR, CSC, BSR, BSC, including rectangular layouts, zero extents, batched independent patterns, hybrid dense tails, zero stored blocks, int32 or int64 compressed pointers, and the scalar sparse_dim == 0 form whose stored entries are summed) into a dense strided tensor of logical shape self.shape; stored values and indices are only read and must not be rewritten, reordered or re-strided, and writes must not escape into a view's backing allocation. For a strided input with dtype omitted the tests assert the identical input object is returned (res_out is inp), which keeps the view geometry, storage offset and lazy neg/conj flags; with dtype supplied the op behaves like Tensor.to and may compact a stepped or column-sliced stride, and the tests compare the output stride, is_neg and is_conj with the native result, assert the output device equals the input device, and check the output dtype through the shared comparison. Passing dtype together with a sparse input is rejected by the native op. masked_grad is keyword-only: the tests run the sparse-leaf backward with it omitted, True and False and compare the resulting sparse gradient with the native gradient on layout, sparse_dim, dense_dim, nnz, coordinates and stored values, so no specific coordinate-count effect is asserted. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract: it defines the overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation behavior, and coverage must not be narrowed to this representative signature.
